title: How Zep Context Graphs keep two timelines for every fact
summary: When a fact changes, a Zep Context Graph keeps the old one with an end date. Agents can see what was true on any date, and when each fact was added.
body_markdown:
Many data agents trust the newest context they can find. Of the 15 internal data agents described in[Metadata is the easy part of a data context layer](https://www.getzep.com/blog/metadata-easy-part-data-context-layer/) , 10 check their context for staleness, and each check tests how recent the context is. A new message, though, can describe a change that applies only from a certain date.


In an example from that post, a data migration in September 2025 changes the key that joins orders to accounts, and a data engineer announces the change in a chat message a week later. An analyst then asks for revenue by account for the first quarter of 2025. The chat message is the newest context about the join key, so an agent that trusts recency applies the new key to orders from before the migration. The query runs and the numbers look plausible, but they are wrong.


Fact about the join key When it was true When it was added


Orders join on` account_id` Until the September 2025 migration January 2025, from a runbook


Orders join on` account_uuid` From the September 2025 migration A week later, from chat


The newest fact about the join key is not the one that applied to first-quarter orders.


The table also shows a second problem: the new key reached the graph a week after it took effect. When a team reviews an answer from that week, it needs to know whether the agent ignored the new key or never had it. A Zep Context Graph keeps both dates on every fact, so the team can tell.


## How Zep timestamps each fact


Each fact in a Zep Context Graph has two timelines. The event timeline records when the fact was true in the world, and the system timeline records when Zep learned it. Zep extracts facts from each episode that you add: a message, a text document, or a JSON business record. Each fact is an edge that connects the entities in the fact, and each edge has four timestamps, two for each timeline.


Timestamp Timeline Meaning


` valid_at` Event time When the fact started to be true


` invalid_at` Event time When the fact stopped being true


` created_at` System time When Zep learned the fact


` expired_at` System time When Zep learned that the fact stopped being true


The four timestamps on each fact in a Context Graph.


A database that keeps both timelines is called bitemporal. With the event timeline, an agent can answer "which join key applied to orders in the first quarter?" With the system timeline, a team can answer "which join key did the graph hold on the day a board report ran?" The two answers differ when Zep receives a fact late or receives a correction after a report.


## How reference_time dates a fact


` reference_time` is the time when the source event happened, for example the time when a message was sent or the start time of a meeting. You set` reference_time` on each episode and each message. If you do not set` reference_time` , Zep uses the ingestion time.


In this example, a data runbook from January 2025 says which key joins orders to accounts. Priya, a data engineer, posts a message about a change on Monday, September 15. You add both as episodes, each with the time when it was written:


PYTHON


```text
from   zep_cloud.client  import   Zep     client = Zep(api_key= "YOUR_API_KEY"  )     # A line from the data runbook, written in January 2025   client.graph.episode.add(       "YOUR_GRAPH_UUID"  ,       type  = "text"  ,      data= "As of January 10, 2025, orders join to accounts on account_id."  ,      reference_time= "2025-01-10T12:00:00Z"  ,  )     # Priya's message in the data team chat, sent on Monday, September 15, 2025   client.graph.episode.add(       "YOUR_GRAPH_UUID"  ,       type  = "text"  ,      data=(           "Data team chat, from Priya (data engineer): Since last Monday, "            "orders join to accounts on account_uuid instead of account_id."       ),      reference_time= "2025-09-15T16:20:00Z"  ,  )
```


A model reads the text of the episode and uses` reference_time` to resolve relative dates such as "last week" or "two years ago". In the example, Priya's message is from Monday, September 15, 2025, and the change applies "since last Monday". Zep sets` valid_at` on the new join-key facts to September 8, 2025.


Zep applies the same rules to other kinds of statements:


- A fact in the present tense, such as "orders join on account_uuid", starts at the` reference_time` of its episode.
- A fact that states an end, such as "the discount applies until March 31", gets that date as` invalid_at` .
- A plan or a deadline, such as "we will move the join next month", starts at` reference_time` . Zep keeps the future date in the fact text and does not use a deadline as` invalid_at` .


Zep dates each statement from its reference time, and a plan's date does not end the fact.


## When a new fact contradicts an old fact


When Zep adds a fact, a model compares it with related facts in the graph. If the model finds a contradiction, Zep compares the two` valid_at` dates. When the new fact starts later, the old fact gets an` invalid_at` equal to the new fact's` valid_at` , and an` expired_at` equal to the current time. The old fact stays in the graph.


After Priya's message, the graph contains two facts about the join key:


- Orders join on` account_id` : valid from January 10, 2025, to September 8, 2025, and expired when Zep read the chat message.
- Orders join on` account_uuid` : valid from September 8, 2025, with no end date.


An agent gets the old key for a question about the first quarter of 2025, and the new key for a question about today. Each fact keeps a link to its[source episode](https://www.getzep.com/blog/how-zep-tracks-provenance-in-agent-memory/) , so a person or an agent can see what changed and why.


The order of ingestion does not change the validity dates. A backfill can deliver an old fact after the fact that replaced it. When the graph already holds a contradicting fact that starts later, Zep ends the incoming fact on that start date. The event timeline comes out the same in either order, and only` created_at` and` expired_at` show the order in which Zep read the sources.


## Querying facts by date


The event timeline answers what was true at a given time, and the system timeline answers what Zep knew at that time. At 9:00 on September 15, seven hours before Priya's message, the two give different answers. On the event timeline,` account_id` had already stopped being true, because the migration happened the week before. On the system timeline, the graph still held` account_id` as current, because Zep had not read the message yet. Graph search with date filters queries each timeline:


PYTHON


```text
from   datetime  import   datetime, timezone  from   zep_cloud.types  import   DateFilter, DateFilterGroup, DateFilters, EdgeSearchFilters     def    search  ( *conditions  ):       return   client.graph.search_edges(           "YOUR_GRAPH_UUID"  ,          query= "Which key joins orders to accounts?"  ,          filters=EdgeSearchFilters(              date_filters=DateFilters(any_of=[DateFilterGroup(all_of= list  (conditions))])          ),      )     def    true_on  ( t  ):       # The fact started on or before t, and it has no end or it ended after t.       started = DateFilter(field= "valid_at"  , operator= "lte"  , value=t)      no_end = search(started, DateFilter(field= "invalid_at"  , operator= "is_null"  ))      later_end = search(started, DateFilter(field= "invalid_at"  , operator= "gt"  , value=t))       return   [*no_end, *later_end]     # Event timeline: the join key for first-quarter orders   q1_facts = true_on(datetime( 2025  ,  3  ,  31  , tzinfo=timezone.utc))     # Event timeline: the join key today   current_facts = true_on(datetime.now(timezone.utc))     # System timeline: the facts that Zep has closed   closed_facts = search(DateFilter(field= "expired_at"  , operator= "is_not_null"  ))
```


For the first quarter,` true_on` returns the` account_id` fact, which is valid from January 10 to September 8, 2025. For today, it returns the` account_uuid` facts, which are valid from September 8. The closed-facts search returns the` account_id` fact. Its` created_at` is the time when Zep read the runbook, and its` expired_at` is the time when Zep read Priya's message. When you run this example, the two times are only seconds apart, because the code adds both episodes at once. A team can compare` expired_at` with the time of a report to find the facts that changed after the report ran. The system timeline starts when you start sending data to Zep. For history loaded in a backfill,` created_at` is the day of the backfill.


The Context Block that an agent retrieves also includes the` valid_at` and` invalid_at` dates of each fact, so the agent sees the event timeline without a filter.


## Setting reference_time for each source


Zep calculates the validity dates from` reference_time` . For each source, send the time of the original event:


1. For chat and email, send the time when the message was sent.
2. For meeting transcripts, send the start time of the meeting.
3. For business records, send the time of the event that the record describes, such as the signature date of a contract.
4. For a backfill with the[Batch API](https://www.getzep.com/blog/the-batch-api-load-large-datasets/) , send the original time on every item. Without` reference_time` , a fact with no explicit date in the text starts on the day of the backfill.


## Getting started with both timelines


A recency check tells an agent which context is newest. The two timelines tell it which fact applied in the period of the question, and what the graph knew at the time. Every fact in a Zep Context Graph has both. Send` reference_time` with each episode and message, and query either timeline with date filters. The[facts documentation](https://help.getzep.com/v4/facts) describes the four timestamps, and the[graph search documentation](https://help.getzep.com/v4/searching-the-graph) covers date filters.


## FAQ


What is the difference between reference_time and valid_at?


` reference_time` is a value that you send with an episode: the time when the message was sent or the event occurred.` valid_at` is a value that Zep calculates for each fact extracted from the episode. Zep uses` reference_time` as the anchor to resolve relative dates in the text. A message sent today about "last week" gives a fact with a` valid_at` in the previous week.


What happens if I do not set reference_time?


Zep uses the ingestion time as the reference time. For live data, the ingestion time is near the event time, and the difference is small. For historical data, a fact with no explicit date in the text gets a` valid_at` near the day of ingestion. When two such facts contradict, Zep can close the newer fact instead of the older fact. Set` reference_time` on each item when you load history.


Does Zep delete a fact that a newer fact contradicts?


Zep keeps the old fact. Zep sets the` invalid_at` of the old fact to the start date of the new fact, and sets the` expired_at` of the old fact to the time when Zep found the contradiction. An agent can still retrieve the old fact for a question about the period when the old fact was true.


What is the difference between invalid_at and expired_at?


` invalid_at` is on the event timeline: the time when the fact stopped being true in the world.` expired_at` is on the system timeline: the time when Zep learned that the fact stopped being true. A rule that changed in March and appeared in a chat message in May has an` invalid_at` in March and an` expired_at` in May.


How do I find the facts that were true on a given date?


Search edges with date filters. A fact was true at time T if its` valid_at` is on or before T and its` invalid_at` is empty or after T. One filter can't combine the empty check and the date check on` invalid_at` , so send two searches that both keep` valid_at` on or before T: one with` invalid_at` empty, and one with` invalid_at` after T. For the facts that Zep held at T, run the same pair with` created_at` in place of` valid_at` and` expired_at` in place of` invalid_at` .
